beats.title: Random soup
beats.text: Eleven thousand epochs in, the soup is still close to random: it holds 131,071 different programs among its 131,072. About 2.3% share one instruction pattern (gold), which does not copy itself.

beats.title: First copiers
beats.text: Family A appears at epoch 11,537 and holds 8.6% of the soup 48 epochs later. Its copies write over everything, including the gold pattern, which drops from 2.3% to 0.2%.

beats.title: Poisoned by its own zeros
beats.text: Family A’s commonest program carries 19 zero bytes, and every copy plants them in the soup: zero bytes rise from 0.4% to 12.6% by epoch 11,713. Family A’s loop stops at a zero it is about to overwrite, so at that level about 3 copies in 10,000 finish. Family A falls to 0.07% by epoch 11,761.

beats.title: Family B sweeps
beats.text: Family B appears at epoch 11,761 and holds 47% of the soup at 11,793 and 74% at 11,825. Its loop checks the byte it has just written, and its commonest program has no zero bytes, so zeros cannot stop it; its copies overwrite them, and zero bytes fall to 1.2% by 11,809. High-order entropy, logged every 128 epochs, first passes 1 at 11,777: the paper’s takeover.

beats.title: Two families share the soup
beats.text: With the zeros cleared, family A comes back, to 11.4% by epoch 12,545, and plants its zeros again (7.2% of bytes). Family B eases from a peak of 76% to 66%. The counted run ends here, 512 epochs after the takeover was confirmed.

summary.takeover_verdict: none: curtailed at 4 of 10 main seeds (amendment 1)
summary.collapse_detail: entropy above 1 at 11,777, distinct programs below half at 11,905

checked: The page’s JavaScript port of the rules and of the replication check agrees with cubff on 30,000 tapes and 3,000 checks.
The seed 2 views come from a bit-for-bit rerun of the counted run from its epoch 9,216 checkpoint; the rerun’s distinct-program counts match the run’s own logs at 11,777, 11,905 and 12,033.
Both family programs shown copy themselves: family A scores 63 of 64 on the replication check, family B 64, and family B’s back-to-front copy also 64.

The zero-byte mechanism, measured directly with 20,000 test partners each: family A finishes 80% of copies against a soup with 0.4% zero bytes and 0.03% at 12.5%; family B finishes all of them at both.

Sham seed 1, with the two copy instructions disabled, ran all 16,384 epochs: high-order entropy never rose above zero, and no two of its 131,072 programs were ever identical. It was interrupted once by a workspace restart and resumed from a checkpoint; the seven logs the two parts share are identical.
Chance calibration: 10,000,000 uniform random programs through the replication check, 0 scoring 48 or more. The 2026 paper’s rate predicts about 0.3.
unchecked: Stage 1’s main criterion: only 4 of the 10 pre-registered main seeds ran, so it gets no verdict.
The 24.8-bit chance cost of a single replicator is the 2026 paper’s figure; 10 million programs can only show it is not much smaller.
Families are grouped by instruction pattern with a tolerance of a few edits. That grouping is description, chosen after the run, and not part of the pre-registration.
The 3D layout squashes 640 dimensions into three and keeps 9% of the variation, so distances in it are rough.
note: Sham seed 1 was stopped at epoch 4,993 when the workspace restarted, and resumed from its epoch 4,096 checkpoint; the runs are deterministic, and the logs where the two parts overlap are identical.
